sections.Kurzabstract: The ESRD-SCL is a disease-specific self-report instrument for assessing the psychological and physiological quality of life of patients after kidney transplantation, with a focus on the side effects of therapy with immunosuppressants. It comprises the scales: (1) Reduced physical functioning (10 items), (2) Reduced cognitive functioning (8 items), (3) Cardiac and renal dysfunction (7 items), (4) Cortisone side effects (5 items), (5) Increased hair and gum growth (5 items), (6) Transplantation-associated psychological burden (8 items) and (7) the Global Score (= mean of all 43 items). Reliability: Reliability (according to Cronbach's alpha) lies between alpha = .76 (scale 3) and alpha = .97 (scale 1). Validity: Validity was demonstrated by correlations with the SF-36 and with sociodemographic and clinical variables.
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The End-Stage Renal Disease Symptom Checklist - Transplantation Module (ESRD-SCL; Franke et al., 2000) is a disease-specific self-report instrument for assessing the psychological and physiological quality of life of patients after kidney transplantation, with a focus on the side effects of therapy with immunosuppressants.
sections.Aufbau:
The burden with regard to the 43 statements is rated on a five-point Likert scale (0 = not at all to 4 = very much) and comprises the scales:
(1) Reduced physical functioning (10 items),
(2) Reduced cognitive functioning (8 items),
(3) Cardiac and renal dysfunction (7 items),
(4) Cortisone side effects (5 items),
(5) Increased hair and gum growth (5 items),
(6) Transplantation-associated psychological burden (8 items),
(7) and the Global Score (= mean of all 43 items).
To answer the questions, the test person should be able to act in a suitable test environment.
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The test construction is based on classical test theory. In the German-speaking area, psychological burden is very often assessed with the SCL-90-R (Franke, 2002) and health-related quality of life often with the generic questionnaire on health status (SF-36; Bullinger & Kirchberger, 1998), although the specific burdens of patients with kidney disease are not taken into account. Experts therefore compiled 79 items that are relevant for this patient group. Items that burdened more than 20% of patients were examined by factor analysis. The final instrument comprises six scales and 43 items as well as a seventh scale that gives the overall sum score.
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: Reliability (according to Cronbach's alpha) lies between alpha = .76 (scale 3) and alpha = .97 (scale 1).
Validity: Validity was demonstrated by correlations with the SF-36 and with sociodemographic and clinical variables.
Norms: No norming of the instrument is available.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: Completing the questionnaire takes between 5 and 10 minutes.
sections.Bewertung:
The instrument is disease-specific and is suitable for assessing burden in kidney transplant recipients. With only 43 items, six dimensions of the disease-specific burden of kidney transplant recipients as well as general psychological burden are assessed in only 5 to 10 minutes, so that the survey also appears reasonable. Administration objectivity is ensured by standardized instructions. Raw scale scores are formed by averaging the items belonging to a scale; item transformations are not necessary. Reference values from various samples are available for judging the level of burden, so that scoring objectivity and interpretation objectivity are ensured. The transparency of the items is high. As with any self-report questionnaire, responses can be faked.
The ESRD-SCL asks about the current burden of kidney transplant recipients, so that the instrument is suitable for repeated measurement. The instrument was constructed for the target group and is available in various languages.
